criteria.statement: Given a feature state dir whose ledger holds one unfiled waived row and a `stack.md` declaring a reachable tracker, `node .claude/lib/waived-defects.js gate --state-dir <dir> --stack <stack.md>` files exactly one issue, labelled `defect`, whose title carries the criterion id and statement, and prints JSON with keys `ok`, `filed`, `already`, `failed` and `ok: true`
criteria.cites: item 1: "For each unfiled one it files one issue in the declared tracker, labelled `defect`, titled with the criterion id and statement"; "It prints `{ ok, filed, already, failed }`"
criteria.evidence: stdout of the gate run (the JSON object) plus the stub `gh` call log showing one `issue create` with `--label defect` and a title containing the criterion id and statement

criteria.statement: The issue body the gate files carries the criterion statement, the failure, its evidence, the feature, TRD, branch and ledger row, and the verbatim line "Shipped waived under `Blocking: must-pass only` (verification.md §5c). This issue stays open until someone decides not to fix it; no Ensemble step closes it."
criteria.cites: item 1: "whose body carries the criterion statement, the failure, its evidence, the feature/TRD/branch/ledger row, and the line …"
criteria.evidence: the issue body as received by the stub `gh` (call log or captured `--body`/`--body-file` content), containing each field and the verbatim sentence

criteria.statement: Run with `--closed-by owner`, the gate words the body's waiver line "Waived under … when the feature was closed by its owner" instead of "Shipped waived under …"
criteria.cites: item 1: "(`--closed-by owner`, the `/close-feature` path, words it "Waived under … when the feature was closed by its owner", since an abandoned feature shipped nothing.)"
criteria.evidence: issue body captured by the stub `gh` for a gate run with `--closed-by owner`, containing "when the feature was closed by its owner" and not "Shipped waived"

criteria.statement: After filing, the gate records the issue URL on the waived row as an append-only `filed <url>` resolve marker in the ledger; no existing ledger line is rewritten
criteria.cites: item 1: "It then records the URL on the row (an append-only `filed <url>` resolve marker, `file-followups`' own convention)"
criteria.evidence: `discovered.jsonl` before and after the gate run: the original lines unchanged byte-for-byte, plus an appended marker naming the criterion and `filed <url>` with the URL the stub returned

criteria.statement: A project whose `stack.md` declares `Tracker: none` and whose ledger holds no waived row passes the gate (`ok: true`) and the tracker is never consulted
criteria.cites: item 1: "It reads the ledger FIRST and looks at the tracker only when an unfiled waived row exists, so a project with `Tracker: none` and no waived rows closes exactly as today"
criteria.evidence: gate stdout showing `ok: true` and an empty stub `gh` call log for that run

criteria.statement: A criterion that had a `[non-blocking]` row but whose latest row is a later `met` row is not filed
criteria.cites: item 1: "a criterion a later pass retired with a `met` row is not filed"
criteria.evidence: gate stdout for a ledger with `[non-blocking]` then `met` rows for one criterion, showing it in neither `filed` nor `failed`, and a stub `gh` call log with no `issue create` for it

criteria.statement: When an issue cannot be filed (tracker create fails), the gate prints `ok: false` with that row in `failed` and the reason it could not be filed
criteria.cites: item 1: "`ok: false` means no close record is written … naming each row (its criterion and summary) and why it could not be filed"
criteria.evidence: gate stdout from a run where the stub `gh` exits non-zero on `issue create`: `ok: false`, `failed` entry naming the criterion and a reason

criteria.statement: An issue that was created but whose `filed <url>` marker could not be written is reported in `failed` with its URL printed
criteria.cites: item 1: "An issue created whose marker could not be written is `failed` with its URL printed, so the refusal names it"
criteria.evidence: gate stdout from a run where the ledger is unwritable after `issue create` succeeds: `ok: false`, a `failed` entry carrying the stub-returned URL

criteria.statement: `/audit-build`, at its close step, runs the gate with `--state-dir .trd-state/<feature>` and `--stack` before writing `closed.json`; when the gate passes, the feature closes
criteria.cites: item 1: "Before writing `closed.json`, both `/audit-build` (its close step) and `/close-feature` run `node .claude/lib/waived-defects.js gate …`"
criteria.evidence: transcript of a headless `/audit-build` session in a fixture repo showing the gate invocation preceding the `closed.json` write, and `closed.json` present afterwards

criteria.statement: `/close-feature` runs the gate (with `--closed-by owner`) before writing `closed.json`; when the gate passes, the feature closes
criteria.cites: item 1: "both `/audit-build` (its close step) and `/close-feature` run …"; "(`--closed-by owner`, the `/close-feature` path …)"
criteria.evidence: transcript of a headless `/close-feature` session in a fixture repo showing the gate invocation with `--closed-by owner` preceding the `closed.json` write

criteria.statement: When the gate returns `ok: false`, `/audit-build` writes no `closed.json`, opens no PR, and ends `COMMAND STUCK` naming each unfiled row (criterion and summary) and why it could not be filed; its `Next:` names fixing the tracker, or filing by hand and running `waived-defects.js record-filed`, then re-running `/audit-build` (never `/close-feature`)
criteria.cites: item 1: "`ok: false` means **no close record is written** … no PR is opened, and the command ends `COMMAND STUCK`, naming each row …"; "The way out of a refusal, named in the STUCK `Next:` … re-run the same command — `/audit-build` after an audit refusal, never `/close-feature`"
criteria.evidence: fixture `/audit-build` session transcript with a failing stub `gh`: final lines `COMMAND STUCK: /audit-build`, each criterion id named, `Next:` naming `record-filed` and `/audit-build`; directory listing showing no `closed.json`; stub `gh` log with no `pr create`

criteria.statement: When the gate returns `ok: false`, `/close-feature` writes no `closed.json` and ends `COMMAND STUCK` naming each unfiled row and why, with a `Next:` naming the way out
criteria.cites: item 1: same refusal sentence, applied to "both" commands
criteria.evidence: fixture `/close-feature` session transcript with a failing stub `gh`: `COMMAND STUCK: /close-feature`, each criterion named, `Next:` line; listing showing no `closed.json`

criteria.statement: On a re-audit of an already-closed feature whose gate refuses, the existing `closed.json` is removed so the feature is not left closed with an unfiled row
criteria.cites: item 1: "on a re-audit of an already-closed feature, the existing `closed.json` is removed — deleting it is the documented way to reopen"
criteria.evidence: fixture state dir listing before (`closed.json` present) and after a refused `/audit-build` (absent), with the session's STUCK banner

criteria.statement: On a refusal, both `/audit-build` and `/close-feature` still perform the records-ref write, so `filed <url>` markers of rows that were filed in that run survive
criteria.cites: item 1: "The records-ref write still runs on a refusal, in both commands, so the `filed <url>` markers of rows that WERE filed survive a temporary worktree"
criteria.evidence: fixture session transcripts of a partly-failed refusal in each command showing the `record-ref.js write` invocation, and `git show refs/ensemble/records/<slug>` ledger content containing the `filed <url>` marker of the row that was filed

criteria.statement: `read-blocking-policy --stack <stack.md>` with `Blocking: must-pass only` declared returns `policy: 'all'`, `declared: 'must-pass'` and a `waiverRefused` reason for each of the 4 tracker states: absent, `none`, unparseable, and a GitHub tracker a read-only `gh repo view` cannot reach
criteria.cites: item 2: "When the declared policy is `must-pass` and the tracker is absent, `none`, unparseable, or (GitHub) not reachable by a read-only `gh repo view`, it returns `policy: 'all'` with `declared: 'must-pass'` and a `waiverRefused` reason"
criteria.evidence: four CLI transcripts (one per tracker state) of `read-blocking-policy` output, each showing `policy`, `declared` and a non-empty `waiverRefused`

criteria.statement: With `must-pass` declared and a reachable GitHub tracker, `read-blocking-policy --stack` keeps `policy: 'must-pass'` and reports no `waiverRefused`
criteria.cites: item 2: the refusal applies only "when … the tracker is absent, `none`, unparseable, or … not reachable"
criteria.evidence: CLI transcript of `read-blocking-policy` with a stub `gh repo view` that succeeds: `policy` is `must-pass`, `waiverRefused` absent or null

criteria.statement: `/implement-trd` (its §8.1a policy read) and `/verify-build` both pass `--stack` to `read-blocking-policy` and hand its `waiverRefused` to the verification workflow as `blockingNote` beside `blocking`
criteria.cites: item 2: "Both `/implement-trd` §8.1a and `/verify-build` pass `--stack` and hand `waiverRefused` to the workflow as a new arg `blockingNote` (string or null) beside `blocking`"
criteria.evidence: fixture `/verify-build` session transcript (Tracker: none, must-pass declared) showing the `--stack` argument and the workflow args carrying `blockingNote`; the same for the `/implement-trd` verification step

criteria.statement: When the waiver is refused, a failing criterion that proves no must-pass objective blocks: the run is not `satisfied` and lists no non-blocking failures
criteria.cites: item 2: title "No tracker, no waiver"; policy returned as `'all'`; report line "every failing criterion blocks"
criteria.evidence: verification run state / report from a fixture with Tracker: none, must-pass declared and one failing ordinary criterion: outcome not `satisfied`, no `nonBlocking` entries

criteria.statement: The verification report carries one `**Blocking**:` header line reading "must-pass only is declared but not applied: <reason>; every failing criterion blocks" when `blockingNote` is present, and a report rendered without `blockingNote` is byte-identical to one rendered before this change
criteria.cites: item 2: "`renderReport` renders one `**Blocking**:` header line from `input.blockingNote` (…), gated on its presence so every other report stays byte-identical"
criteria.evidence: two rendered reports from the same input with and without `blockingNote`: the first contains the line with the reason; the second diffed against the pre-change render of that input shows no difference

criteria.statement: The `**Blocking**:` line survives every re-render of the report — fix rounds and the re-proof retry
criteria.cites: item 2: "The workflow carries it into every report input the way it carries `nonBlocking` … Because it is rendered, not patched, every re-render (fix rounds, the re-proof retry) keeps it"
criteria.evidence: report file from a run with `blockingNote` set that went through at least one fix round, containing the `**Blocking**:` line in its final rendering

criteria.statement: The command readout's DECISIONS section states that must-pass only was declared but not applied, and why, when the waiver is refused
criteria.cites: item 2: "The readout's DECISIONS says the same"
criteria.evidence: fixture `/verify-build` session transcript: the DECISIONS section contains the not-applied statement with its reason

criteria.statement: A criterion that already has a recorded issue URL is never filed again: a resumed run, a fix round's `recordNonBlockingFollowups`, a repeated gate, and `file-followups` all leave it unfiled, and a newer waived row for it is marked with the same URL rather than producing a new issue or a new open ledger row
criteria.cites: item 1: "'Never twice' is per criterion: a criterion with any recorded URL is never filed again; a newer waived row for it is marked with that same URL"; item 3: "`recordNonBlockingFollowups` treats a `[non-blocking]` row whose issue is already filed as recorded (it reads resolved rows too), so no new open row appears for it"; "`file-followups` files a `[non-blocking]` row only through `waived-defects.js gate`, which skips a row with a recorded URL"
criteria.evidence: ledger and stub `gh` call log across: a gate run, a second gate run, a `recordNonBlockingFollowups` call for the same criterion, a new waived row then a gate run, and a `file-followups` step run — exactly one `issue create` in the whole log; the second gate's stdout lists the criterion in `already`; the newer row carries `filed <same url>`; no new open `[non-blocking]` row after `recordNonBlockingFollowups`

criteria.statement: After a refusal, filing the issue by hand and running `waived-defects.js record-filed --state-dir <dir> --ref <ref> --url <url>` lets the next gate pass without filing that criterion
criteria.cites: item 1: "file the issue by hand and run `node .claude/lib/waived-defects.js record-filed --state-dir <dir> --ref <ref> --url <url>` (any tracker), then re-run the same command"
criteria.evidence: ledger showing the `filed <url>` marker written by `record-filed`, followed by gate stdout with `ok: true`, the criterion in `already`, and no `issue create` in the stub `gh` log for that run

criteria.statement: `waived-defects.js` never closes, edits or comments on an issue: across every gate run its runner is handed only `issue create`, `label list`, `label create` and `repo view`; and the document governing `close-issue` carries a sentence that a later feature written to fix a waived-defect issue may cite and close it on ship
criteria.cites: item 4: "`waived-defects.js` runs no close, edit or comment command (its runner is only ever handed `issue create`, `label list`, `label create` and `repo view`, which a test asserts by recording every call)"; "The contract gains one sentence saying so"
criteria.evidence: the stub `gh` call log accumulated over all gate runs above, containing no subcommand outside those four; the sentence located in the `close-issue` contract text

criteria.statement: When the close succeeds having filed waived rows, both `/audit-build` and `/close-feature` list each filed issue's URL with its criterion in the readout's STATE section
criteria.cites: item 5: "Filed waived rows drop out of the DISCOVERED summary (resolved rows are hidden), so both close commands list each filed issue's URL with its criterion in STATE"
criteria.evidence: fixture session transcripts of a successful close for each command: STATE section naming each criterion id beside its stub-returned URL
